predictions.title: Launch Price

predictions.poll_question: Is $79.99 worth it for GTA VI?

predictions.title: GTA VI Is the Cheapest GTA at Launch in Real Terms
predictions.unit: cheaper than GTA III ($90.75) in 2026 dollars
predictions.basis: GTA VI's confirmed $79.99 launch price is 11.9% cheaper in real 2026 terms than GTA III ($90.75) in 2026 dollars. CPI-U adjusted comparison: GTA III ($49.99 in 2001 = $90.75 in 2026), GTA VC ($89.34), GTA SA ($85.08), GTA IV ($89.58) all cost more in real terms than GTA VI's $79.99.
predictions.prediction_method: CPI-U adjusted price comparison — US Bureau of Labor Statistics + official Rockstar/Take-Two pricing
prediction_inputs: franchise/cpi.json → base_cpi + title CPI year values

prediction_range.low: Confirmed — math is not a prediction
prediction_range.high: Confirmed — math is not a prediction

predictions.source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI-U · Rockstar/Take-Two official pricing

predictions.basis: Weekly bonus events are the primary live-service engagement loop in GTA Online, operating continuously since 2017. Take-Two earnings reports consistently cite live events as a key monetisation driver. The weekly event cadence is a structural feature of the MMT sovereign model.

predictions.title: GTA Online Layer Launches at or Near Day 1
predictions.value: GTA Online VI launches within 30 days of story mode
predictions.basis: Take-Two's revenue model cannot sustain a 6-month GTA Online delay (as occurred with GTA V in 2013). Shark Card revenue is the primary live-service income stream. Each month of delay costs Take-Two significant recurring revenue at the highest-demand period in franchise history.
prediction_inputs: Take-Two revenue dependency on Shark Cards

prediction_range.high: 30-day delay maximum

predictions.source: GTAVI.AI Economic Model Analysis

predictions.title: No Loans at Maze Bank — Savings Only
predictions.value: Savings hold GTA$ but credit/loans remain absent
predictions.basis: Franchise-wide pattern: savings never compound in any GTA title. Maze Bank in GTA Online is explicitly decorative (no credit). No title has ever introduced a loan or credit mechanic — introducing one would fundamentally alter the Shark Card revenue model by reducing SC purchase urgency.

prediction_range.high: Savings with nominal interest, still no credit

predictions.source: GTAVI.AI Economic Model Analysis

predictions.basis: GTA V established per-character financial independence (Michael, Trevor, Franklin each hold separate balances). Two protagonists in GTA VI naturally extends this — particularly relevant for a multi-region model where each character may operate primarily in one region.

prediction_range.high: Fully independent financial states, separate business portfolios per character

predictions.title: Rockstar Expected to Nerf Payouts Within 6 Months
predictions.value: First nerf within 6 months
predictions.basis: GTA Online has delivered a major payout nerf within 6–18 months of every high-yield activity launch since 2015. Structural incentive: high yields suppress Shark Card sales. The question is not if GTA VI nerfs occur, but when.

predictions.title: GTA VI Megalodon Shark Card launch price
predictions.basis: GTA Online's Megalodon Shark Card has been $99.99 since 2013. CPI adjustment to 2026 (~35% inflation) implies a real-terms equivalent of ~$135, suggesting a nominal increase is economically justified. Take-Two has historically kept nominal prices flat while engineering real-terms inflation via payout nerfs. A price increase at the launch of a new title would be the cleanest reset point.

prediction_range.high: $119.99 (CPI reset)

predictions.source: GTAVI.AI Economic Model Analysis — franchise/cpi.json + shark-cards.json

predictions.title: Top Hourly Yield at GTA VI Online Launch
predictions.value: ~$3M–5M GTA$/hr
predictions.basis: GTA Online launched at ~$250K/hr in 2013 and reached $2M/hr (Cayo Perico, 2020) before nerfs. The 8× yield growth over 7 years reflects both inflation and content scaling. GTA VI Online inherits the MMT sovereign model at a structurally higher yield floor. Historical nerf cadence suggests yields above $5M/hr are politically unsustainable for Rockstar's Shark Card model.

prediction_range.low: $2M/hr (continuation of current GTA Online S-tier floor)
prediction_range.high: $8M/hr (new heist format with full MMT rebalancing)

predictions.source: GTAVI.AI Economic Model Analysis — meta-history.json + revenue-tiers.json

predictions.basis: Multi-region Eurozone analogy — two structurally different regions sharing one currency (GTA$) historically produce purchasing power divergence. Urban density correlates with higher prices across GTA franchise history.

prediction_range.high: 25–40% price premium in VC

prediction_range.high: Fully tiered regional SC denominations

predictions.title: GTA VI Endgame Cost via Shark Cards — 12 Months
predictions.basis: GTA Online's endgame cost via Shark Cards grew from ~$18.75 (2013) to ~$437.50 (2026) — a 23× increase over 13 years. GTA VI Online starts with a reset baseline but inherits the same structural incentive to expand the aspirational item stack. The $600–$900 range assumes a 30–100% premium over GTA Online's current endgame.
prediction_inputs: item-catalogue.json → price inflation rate per patch era

prediction_range.high: $1,200 (new high-tier aspirational vehicles + regional DLC stack)

predictions.source: GTAVI.AI Economic Model Analysis — shark-cards.json endgame projection

predictions.basis: RDR2 required manual, animated looting of bodies and environments. Community reports confirm this transfers to GTA VI — drawers, glove boxes, and pockets all searchable individually. Economically: higher time-cost per loot event means per-loot values must be higher to maintain viable ambient income.

prediction_range.high: Mandatory manual looting for all interactions — significantly higher per-loot payouts to compensate

predictions.title: Context-sensitive NPC interactions affect mission access and pricing
predictions.value: NPC interaction system confirmed
predictions.basis: RDR2's greet/antagonize system (hold/tap near NPCs) gave Arthur honour points that unlocked dialogue branches and changed shop prices. Community sources report a direct analogue in GTA VI tied to Lucia and Jason's reputation in different regions. Economically, this creates a dynamic pricing layer over the base GTA$ system — the first time franchise pricing has been protagonist-behaviour-dependent.

prediction_range.high: Full pricing tier system (±20%)

predictions.title: GTA VI will have a Trader-style supply and sell passive income cycle
predictions.value: Passive business cycle confirmed likely
predictions.basis: RDR Online's Trader role (Butcher's Table) is the closest structural precedent to GTA Online's Bunker and MC businesses — supply materials, process product, sell for profit on a 2-hour cycle. Community sources report GTA VI Online will have a resource/goods trading layer in the Leonida economy. The Trader role earned RDR$625 per full delivery, which at franchise income scaling maps to GTA$800K–$1.2M/hr in a GTA VI context.
predictions.prediction_method: RDR Online Trader income scaled by franchise income inflation rate (GTA V → VI)

prediction_range.high: GTA$1.4M/hr (optimised with upgrades)

predictions.source: RDR Online role precedent + community insider reports
predictions.poll_question: Will GTA VI have a Bunker/MC-style supply and sell business cycle?

predictions.title: Eagle Eye threat detection mechanic carries forward into GTA VI
predictions.value: Enhanced perception mode predicted
predictions.basis: RDR2's Eagle Eye (hold R3) highlighted threats, tracks, herbs and collectibles in the environment. GTA V had a limited heightened sense (special ability). Community sources report GTA VI introduces a sustained threat-detection mode for both protagonists — spotting ambushes, tracking targets, and identifying loot containers. Economically, this reduces time-cost of ambient income (looting, hunting) and changes the risk/reward calculation for wanted-level missions.
predictions.prediction_method: RDR2 mechanic transfer analysis — Eagle Eye → GTA VI threat detection

prediction_range.high: Full Eagle Eye clone with tracking and loot detection

predictions.source: Community insider reports + RDR2 Eagle Eye mechanic precedent
predictions.poll_question: Will GTA VI have an Eagle Eye-style threat detection ability?

predictions.title: GTA VI will have a collectible circuit income tier
predictions.value: Collectible economy tier predicted
predictions.basis: RDR Online's Collector role (Madam Nazar) monetised world exploration by turning ambient collectibles into income. 9 full sets worth ~$400 each. GTA Online had hidden packages and collectibles but no income system attached. The GTA VI world — spanning two distinct territories — has the geographic complexity to support a collectible economy. This would be the franchise's first income-generating exploration mechanic, filling the 'ambient explorer' player niche.
predictions.prediction_method: RDR Online Collector income scaled to GTA VI income ceiling + exploration complexity estimate

prediction_range.high: Full collector circuit — GTA$200K–$500K/hr for active hunters

predictions.source: RDR Online Collector role precedent + GTAVI.AI economic model
predictions.poll_question: Will collecting items around the map earn real GTA$ in GTA VI?

predictions.title: A Regional Purchasing Parity Index for GTA VI
predictions.value: GTA-RPP ratio diverges between Vice City and Leonida
predictions.basis: If regional price differentials exist, a single GTA-PPI index will understate inflation for one region. The GTA-RPP — basket cost ÷ top hourly yield, computed per territory — is the essential post-launch metric for this site.

prediction_range.high: GTA-RPP diverges >30% — significant real wage gap between territories

predictions.source: GTAVI.AI Economic Model Analysis
